title: Course Feedback
instructions: Please answer each question in a few sentences. There are no right or wrong answers — honest feedback helps improve the course.
questions: Which topic in this course did you find most challenging, and why?
Describe one concept you understood only after the practical assignments. What made it click?
How has your approach to designing databases or APIs changed since the start of the trimester?
What would you improve about how this course was taught or assessed?
How do you plan to apply what you learned in this course going forward?
answers: Concurrency. Two simultaneous requests can both pass a check and break a rule, so I learned the guarantee has to come from the database: unique keys, transactions and row locks.

Internationalisation. Building the feedback page showed me how to keep all text in locale files, pick the language from ?lang with a safe fallback to English, and format dates for each locale with Intl.DateTimeFormat.
I now let the database enforce rules with constraints, and design APIs with clear REST routes, correct status codes and separate layers with parameterized SQL.
I will protect data with constraints and transactions, move slow work to background workers, and keep business rules in small, testable functions.
thank_you: Thank you! Your feedback has been received.
